Gṛtsamada
------------------------------------------
Gṛtsamada is a ṛṣi or sage to whom the authorship of the second मण्डल of the Ṛgveda is attributed. The name has been defined as one who was both intelligent and happy always.
He was the son of the sage Śunahotra. When he was performing a sacrifice once, असुरस् or demons abducted him. However, on his praying to इन्द्र, इन्द्र rescued him.
He seems to have been the adopted son of Śunaka, a descendant of the sage भृगु. Hence the patronym भार्गव.
According to another version he was the son of वीतहव्य, a क्षत्त्रिय king, who later became a ब्राह्मण.
Gṛtsamada is said to have saved इन्द्र once, from being caught by the असुरस्, by assuming his form and cheating them.
The ṛks (Ṛgvedic mantras) attributed to him are highly poetic.
